forwardNote: the nose points towards -Z; headlights at z < 0, tail lights at z > 0. Positive yaw (rotation about +Y) and positive steering angle turn LEFT.
origin: on the ground plane, midway between the bumpers and on the car centre line (x = 0)

wheelAnimation.spin: wheel_xx_spin.rotation.x -= distanceTravelled / radius   (negative rotation.x = rolling forward, towards -Z)
wheelAnimation.note: hub nodes (wheel_xx) and spin nodes (wheel_xx_spin) have identity rest rotation and their origin at the wheel centre; the axle is the local X axis.

steeringWheel.usage: steering_wheel.rotation.z = +angle turns the wheel counter-clockwise as seen by the driver = steering LEFT (same sign as wheel_f*.rotation.y). Suggested ratio: steering wheel angle = 12 * road-wheel angle, clamp +-450 deg.

headlights.note: position = centre of the projector lens at its front surface; put SpotLights here pointing along direction (dip ~2 deg)

indicators.note: each side = fender repeater + LED cluster in the centre of the round tail lamp. Front indicators: blink the DRL strip amber.

driverEye.note: head position of a ~1.78 m driver; steering wheel is on the LEFT. Hide nothing: the interior is fully modelled.

bonnet.note: just ahead of the windscreen base, shows the top of the bonnet and both front wings

bumper.note: in front of the nose, nothing of the car visible

chase.note: default third-person camera in car space

physics.note: Suggestions. Car space: origin on the ground under the middle of the car, +Y up, nose towards -Z, +X = right.

chassisBox.note: covers the body shell from y=0.3 (below wheel-centre height 0.358, above the 0.1164 m ground clearance) to the top of the rear deck; the lower half of the wheels, the splitter/diffuser lips and the mirrors stick out on purpose

cabinBox.note: optional second collider: windscreen frame / roll-over height

centerOfMass.note: estimate: mid-rear engine, 42 % front / 58 % rear static weight distribution, CoG height ~0.46 m

physics.massNote: kerb weight of the real car this model depicts (for reference)
physics.suspensionTravelNote: visual clearance tyre top -> wheel arch is about 0.06 m front / 0.07 m rear; keep visual bump travel within +-0.05 m

bodyProfile.note: body-paint mesh envelope per 0.2 m slice along Z (yMin/yMax/half width incl. mirrors)

rims.uvMasks: TEXCOORD_0.x = 1 on the machined spoke face + outer lip, TEXCOORD_0.y = 1 on the centre cap

brakeCalipers.note: children of the hub node (wheel_xx), NOT of wheel_xx_spin: they steer but do not rotate with the wheel

badges.note: all brand emblems, scripts and shields of the source model were removed in the build (pass --keep-badges to car-build.mjs to keep them as a separate "badges" mesh)

groundShadow.source: three.js examples/models/gltf/ferrari_ao.png (baked contact shadow / ground AO for this exact model)
groundShadow.placement: child of the car root at the origin, rotation.x = -PI/2 (lies on the ground, y = 0); image top = car nose (-Z)
groundShadow.material: MeshBasicMaterial({ map, blending: MultiplyBlending, toneMapped: false, transparent: true, premultipliedAlpha: true })
notes: white = no darkening; it multiplies whatever is below, so it needs no alpha channel
in r187 WebGPU MultiplyBlending REQUIRES premultipliedAlpha = true
add depthWrite: false and a small polygonOffset (or y = 0.005) when the road is not perfectly flat; fade it out with speed/height if the car can leave the ground

conventions: Keys of "byMaterial" are glTF material names in car.glb / car_lod1.glb. Replace the loaded material of every mesh by the node material built from the entry with the same name.

Vertex colour (COLOR_0, grey) is baked ambient occlusion = sky visibility. Use it as material.aoNode = mix(1, mix(aoFloor, 1, vertexColor().r), ao); never as albedo (set vertexColors = false). aoFloor (default 0) stands in for light bouncing around inside the cabin.
All car surfaces exist twice in LOD0 (second copy with reversed winding). Keep every material FrontSide; never use DoubleSide on LOD0.
Light meshes are driven by emissive only: emissiveNode = emissive colour * intensity(state). Off-state looks come from the base parameters.

tireTread.channels: RGB = tangent-space normal (OpenGL +Y), A = cavity (1 surface .. 0 groove floor)

tireSidewall.channels: RGB = tangent-space normal (OpenGL +Y), A = height (0.5 = base, lettering/ribs > 0.5)

lights.note: intensity multiplies the linear emissive colour; values assume ACES/AgX tone mapping at exposure ~1 and an optional bloom threshold of 1.

drl.note: LED strips in the headlamps; daytime running light. May double as front indicator (amber #ff8a1a, blink).

tail.note: the mesh to make emissive when braking; "tail" level when the lights are on

Body_Color.note: base layer = pigment (+ metallic flakes: per-cell random normal in object space, faded with distance), colour shifts to flopColor at grazing angles, clearcoat keeps the smooth geometric normal

Glass_Gray.note: windscreen + wind stop. alpha = 1 - transmission * (1 - fresnel); CustomBlending One / OneMinusSrcAlpha so reflections are added at full strength; depthWrite false

Lamp_Glass.note: clear headlamp covers and tail-lamp centre lenses

Taillight_Lens.note: smooth red outer lens of the round tail lamps; the fluted inner part (Taillight_Glass) is the emitter

Trim_Black.note: unpainted exterior plastic: diffuser, splitter, strakes, wipers, arch liners, undertray

Grille_Mesh.note: flat panels: procedural diamond mesh (object-space, projected on the dominant axis)

Mirror.note: door mirrors + interior mirror; reflects the environment map only

Exhaust_Tip.note: polished steel; baked AO < 0.45 blends to soot so the inside of the pipes is black

Headlight_Housing.note: satin dark chrome bezels inside the headlamps

Leather.note: black leather: dashboard, doors, seat bolsters, steering wheel rim

Carbon_Fiber.note: 2x2 twill weave, procedural in object space (dominant-axis projection)

metal_gray.note: satin aluminium: pedals, vent bezels, door handles, knobs

Gauge_Face.note: rev counter face (no dial markings in the model)

Tires.note: UV.x = once around, UV.y: 0-0.25 outboard sidewall (bead -> shoulder), 0.25-0.75 tread, 0.75-1 inboard sidewall

Rim.note: UV.x = 1 on the machined spoke face/outer lip (two-tone wheels: raise faceMix), UV.y = 1 on the centre cap

Brake_Disc.note: cross-drilled pattern + radial brushing are procedural in wheel-local polar coordinates; UV = (outer radius, inner radius) constants per disc

lod1Notes: same node names for everything that is animated (wheel_xx, wheel_xx_spin, steering_column, steering_wheel) and for the role meshes that still exist; one layer of triangles only (use shadowSide = DoubleSide when it is used as a shadow caster); tyres keep their UV layout, rims keep the UV masks.
